Electron opened access to space, but 100 launches is just the start. 

There's 55+ Rocket Lab spacecraft in development and production, multiple missions operating on orbit today, and $1b+ worth of launches booked across all three of our rocket programs - Electron, HASTE and Neutron.

We're delivering spacecraft and components to the Moon, Mars, and intend to operate our own constellation and space services for millions of people on Earth.

Our spacecraft just made interplanetary history - twice.

Blue & Gold flawlessly executed powered Earth gravity assists, two days apart, to slingshot our planet and shoot for Mars' orbit.

This is the first time the highly complex maneuver has been executed successfully by spacecraft.

ESCAPADE has proven a new path is possible to make it to Mars outside the typical Earth-to-Mars launch window that occurs every 26 months.

Next ESCAPADE mission milestone: Mars Orbit Insertion, September 2027.

posts.author: rocketlab
posts.text:
Blue and Gold are on their way to Mars!

The twin spacecraft, designed and built by Rocket Lab, for @NASA and @ucbssl's ESCAPADE mission, completed powered Earth gravity assists to each perfectly execute a trans-Mars Injection.

Both spacecraft fired their main engine for 9.5 minutes, hurtling past Earth at more than 10 kilometers per second, to enter an interplanetary cruise phase.

They are due to arrive at the Red Planet in September 2027 to study the Martian atmosphere.

posts.author: rocketlab
posts.text:
It’s a beautiful day to set sail with the next pieces of Neutron flight hardware to Launch Complex 3.

Earlier today we sent Neutron’s Stage 2 and Thrust Module out of the Neutron Factory and onto a barge for transport through Chesapeake Bay to Wallops Island in Virginia. 

Once it arrives, the Thrust Module will go straight onto the launch mount at LC-3 for check outs and the beginning of wider systems demonstrations including integrated fluids tests and module-to-launch-mount interface checkouts. With no strongback on the launch mount by design, Neutron’s Thrust Module is the rocket’s only physical interface to the launch pad, which this upcoming test campaign enables us to test early before the entire vehicle comes together.
